text:
maria: quick heads-up: sketching a less disruptive v1->v2 migration flow. goal: avoid sudden breakage, give customers visibility, and provide fast rollback.

sam: sounds good. high level steps?

maria: 1) telemetry-only period where we run passive analysis on requests mapped to v2 behavior. 2) an opt-in client probe that can be enabled per-org. 3) advisory response headers for non-probe traffic. 4) console migration dashboard + pause button. 5) routing override primitives + global kill-switch.

jordan: probe needs to exercise the exact auth/routing/model selection path under v2 rules. if probes don't include that, we'll miss auth/header parity issues.

praveen: quota/billing implications: probe traffic will inflate request counts unless exempted. we should mark probe calls with a header like `X-RW-Probe:1` and exclude them from billing/quotas.

maria: agreed. also plan to emit `compat.probe.*` metrics and a per-org compat_score metric (percent probes passing).

alex: console needs a per-org migration panel: compat_score over time, top failing endpoints, last failure sample, and a one-click "pause migration for this org (24h)". only org-admins can pause.

tilly-deploy-bot: deploy: compat-probe endpoint rolled to canary fleet (5% hosts) at 09:12UTC :rocket:

sam: for non-SDK clients we should return a structured advisory header instead of changing response codes. e.g., `Warning: 299 Redwood v2-advisory; info=https://redwood/docs/migrate` and `X-RW-Deprecation: v1_header_parsing`.

jordan: agree we should never change 2xx semantics. also probes should include a fallback token in body for clients behind proxies that strip custom headers.

maria: plan: `/v2/compatibility-check` endpoint that returns a compact JSON of flags. SDKs call it by default when `auto_migrate=true`. raw clients can poll it once per deploy.

sam: sample response we discussed:

```
GET /v2/compatibility-check
200 OK
{
  "ok": true,
  "flags": ["auth-ok","header-parse-ok","model-route-ok"],
  "suggested_action": "none"
}
```

maria: SDKs will surface compat_score and let users opt into auto-migrate. question: default `auto_migrate` true or false?

jordan: prefer `false` by default. we need explicit opt-in so we don't silently introduce changes for existing apps.

praveen: ops needs alerts if probe pass rate drops below 95% for any org. also verify parity of token billing when probes are excluded.

alex: UX copy for console banner draft: "Redwood v2 rollout in progress — review your migration dashboard. Click to pause migration for your org. Some clients may receive advisory headers." keep it short.

maria: routing infra note: add per-org routing override entries with TTL and a `force_route_to_v1` boolean. also add a global emergency flag to route everyone to v1 for up to 24h with audit logs.

sam: data/telemetry: store sampled failure traces for privacy. probes should return minimal failure reasons to clients but we store detailed traces for internal debugging only.

jordan: edge case: devices that strip headers (mobile proxies). probes should support a `compat_token` returned from `/compatibility-check` that clients can send in body if headers are not preserved.

maria: good. SDKs will attempt header approach first, then fall back to body token.

praveen: billing: we need an exempt dimension for probe traffic in billing pipeline; coordinate with billing team before rolling probes wide.

maria: added checklist for RFC: probe design, advisory headers, compat endpoint, telemetry schema, quota/billing exemption, routing overrides, console UX, SDK defaults, global kill-switch, permissions. I'll open RFC and tag folks.

maria: opened RFC at https://redwood/intern/rfcs/987  please review by EOW.

sam: I'll draft the telemetry event definitions and compat_score data model.

alex: I'll produce console mockups and permission gating for pause action.

jordan: SDK leads: please comment on feasibility for header+body fallback before EOW.

praveen: billing/ops will review the exempt billing path and emergency rollback playbook.

maria: thanks all. we'll iterate in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
